topStories.headline: Heber Valley Chamber to Break Away From Tourism Office and Go It Alone in 2027
topStories.dek: After nearly 15 years as a joint operation, the Heber Valley Chamber of Commerce will become an independent, business-led organization on January 1.
topStories.body:
The Heber Valley Chamber of Commerce is separating from Wasatch County's Tourism and Economic Development office, ending a partnership that has lasted almost 15 years. Beginning January 1, 2027, the chamber will operate as a fully independent organization governed by an executive-level board and funded through membership fees and events rather than government taxes.

The Tourism and Economic Development office will continue under Executive Director Dallin Koecher with its existing eight-member staff, focusing exclusively on visitor promotion and economic vitality. Its funding will come from transient room taxes and grants, as it does now. Koecher said the split will allow his agency to sharpen its focus while the chamber concentrates on peer-to-peer business relationships.

Chamber Public Relations Manager Jessica Turner said the organization — which currently has about 370 members — plans rebranding efforts and a rollout of a new destination development plan. Turner also identified increased advocacy for workforce housing as a priority going forward.

The chamber hosts a range of annual events open to the broader community, including monthly luncheons, a golf tournament, and tree-lighting celebrations in both Heber City and Midway. Its advisory board draws from local business owners and nonprofit leaders including representatives from the Wasatch Community Foundation and Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory.

topStories.headline: Heber City Honors Its Only Vietnam War Combat Loss With Bronze Plaque and Street Dedication
topStories.dek: A ceremony on November 10 commemorated Lance Cpl. Blaine A. Welch, a Wasatch High graduate killed in action in 1968 — the county's sole service member lost in that war.
topStories.body:
Heber City marked Veterans Week with a formal ceremony honoring Lance Cpl. Blaine A. Welch, the only service member from Wasatch County killed in action during the Vietnam War. A new bronze plaque and a street dedication were installed at the corner of City Hall at 75 North Main Street.

Welch was born and raised in Heber City and graduated from Wasatch High School before enlisting in the United States Marine Corps in 1967. He trained as a scout sniper and was assigned to the 9th Marine Regiment. He was killed in action on August 22, 1968, in Quang Tri Province, South Vietnam, at age 20. He is buried at the Heber City Cemetery.

Mayor Heidi Franco unveiled the plaque and spoke to the crowd about what it represents to the community. Welch's younger brother Brent attended and thanked his brother's friends for continuing to visit Welch's grave and their mother in the decades since his death. United States Marines stood at attention during the national anthem.

The bronze plaque was funded through Heber City's Trail, Arts and Parks tax following a unanimous 5-0 council vote in April to authorize the expenditure. The street dedication names the stretch of road near City Hall in Welch's honor.

topStories.headline: Wilderness Circuit Finals Close Out Heber City's Rodeo Year With Two Nights of Pro Competition
topStories.dek: More than $171,000 in added money was on the line as professional cowboys and cowgirls competed in eight PRCA disciplines at the Wasatch County Event Center on November 6 and 7.
topStories.body:
Professional rodeo came to Heber City for the final time this year as the Wilderness Circuit Finals filled the Wasatch County Event Center on November 6 and 7. The two-night event drew competitors from across the region and marked the last rodeo of the season for the city.

The competition spanned eight disciplines: bareback riding, saddle bronc riding, bull riding, steer wrestling, team roping, tie-down roping, breakaway roping and barrel racing. The event is sanctioned by both the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association and the Women's Professional Rodeo Association, and carried more than $152,000 in added money for the main rodeo plus an additional $19,000 for the standalone breakaway roping competition.

For some competitors the Heber City stop was close to home. One PRCA cowboy entering his third season noted the event put him about 30 minutes from his family's property in Wanship. The Wilderness Circuit Finals are part of a professional rodeo season that runs from October through September each year.

moreNews.headline: County Council to Hear UDOT Bypass Update and Preview 2027 Budget This Month
moreNews.body:
Wasatch County Manager Dustin Grabau said November council meetings would include a progress briefing from UDOT on its environmental impact study for the Heber Valley bypass through the North Fields, along with an introduction to the tentative 2027 county budget. Proposed new positions in the budget include an investigator for the county attorney's office and a code enforcement officer, with additional budget conversations planned throughout the month.

Separately, Heber City and Wasatch County are continuing to work through a plan to consolidate their respective justice courts into a single county-operated court. The Heber City Council has directed staff to negotiate an interlocal agreement with the county, a step that would also require approval from the Utah Judicial Council. City staff has estimated direct justice court costs in the FY 2027 budget at roughly $399,000.
